entities.summary: Frank Friday Fletcher was a United States Navy admiral who served in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. He was awarded the U.S. military's highest decoration, the Medal of Honor, for his actions as commander of navy forces at the Battle of Veracruz, Mexico. The Fletcher-class destroyer, the most produced class of United States Navy destroyers, was named after him. He was also the uncle of Frank Jack Fletcher, another U.S. Navy admiral who also received the Medal of Honor for actions at Veracruz, and who commanded American naval forces at the battles of Coral Sea, Midway, in the Eastern Solomons, and the Aleutian Campaign during World War II.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Frank Friday Fletcher's actions as commander of navy forces at the Battle of Veracruz, Mexico, earned him the Medal of Honor and had significant regional impact during World War I. His legacy also influenced the development of the U.S. Navy's destroyer fleet.
